premise.text: Massage / Physical Therapist at Park, facing Running out of critical supplies, with a Just instinct and a Foolish streak in a Herding mode

jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: Consent Cardio
jokes.joke: I set up at the Park offering free leg stretches to joggers, because I thought, “Everybody looks tense.” It was a Foolish plan. The first guy I approached started sprinting, so I sprinted after him yelling, “I can fix that hamstring!” That’s when I learned wellness becomes a crime at about twelve miles an hour.

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Goose Protocol
jokes.joke: I'm a massage therapist who sets up in the Park on weekends. Sounds peaceful — it is not. Last Sunday I spent forty minutes herding a client's hamstring back where it belongs, and another twenty explaining to a golden retriever that the table is not a buffet. The dog tipped better.

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: Collie Instincts
jokes.joke: I took my new rescue collie to the local park. He absolutely refuses to fetch. His whole life revolves around herding. It sounds adorable, right up until I have to explain to a furious mother why her four toddlers are seamlessly corralled into a tight pentagon by the swingset.

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Parkside Therapy
jokes.joke: Folks, I work as a Massage / Physical Therapist at the Park, and let me tell you it's not the zen paradise I pictured. Last week this stressed executive lies down on my portable table and right as I hit the knot in his back, a frisbee smacks him in the head. He bolts up yelling, and I just shrug and say, 'That's nature's way of saying you need deeper work.'

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Hands Full
jokes.joke: As a Massage / Physical Therapist, I never expected my day to turn into full-on Herding. One client brought three friends who all lined up behind me like I was leading a wellness parade. I tried to stay professional, but nothing kills your authority faster than realizing you’re basically the world’s calmest sheepdog with a folding table.

Solid escalation and the 'twelve miles an hour' line is a genuine payoff with good specificity. The setup is a touch slow but the punchline earns its place.
The pentagon detail is the joke's engine — specific, visual, and unexpected. Doesn't need the premise context to work, which is the mark of a clean standalone.
